query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small volume fraction of Cu to (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 will enhance its structural integrity by forming ductile, crack‐arresting Cu-rich precipitates without altering its inherent caloric properties.
generation.material_initial_state: The pure (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy, which shows a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field conditions but tends to crack under load.
generation.intervention: Introduce a controlled addition of approximately 3–5 vol% Cu into the alloy during melting and solidification so that a ductile Cu-rich phase precipitates within the matrix.
generation.conditions: Process the alloy under the standard synthesis and thermomechanical treatments that yield the baseline microstructure; subsequently, test the samples under the same applied-field, pressure-field, temperature, and loading regimes as the baseline measurements.
generation.structural_mediator: The finely dispersed, ductile Cu-rich precipitates that form at grain boundaries and within the grains.
generation.mechanism: The presence of Cu-rich precipitates is expected to toughen the brittle matrix by bridging micro-cracks and arresting crack propagation. This microstructural reinforcement is anticipated to improve compressive strength and overall integrity while the primary lattice and transformational mechanism responsible for the caloric response remain unperturbed.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the unchanged (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy, the Cu-doped alloy will exhibit increased compressive strength and reduced cracking with maintained caloric performance (i.e., similar entropy change and transformation behavior under applied-field and pressure-field conditions).
generation.baseline: The original (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy with high caloric response but poor mechanical integrity (frequent cracking under load).
generation.boundary: The alloy system remains rare-earth-free, with all processing and testing conditions (applied-field, pressure-field, temperature, and loading regimes) kept consistent with those used for the baseline material.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal Cu addition level may need further adjustment to achieve the best balance between improved toughness and unaltered caloric behavior, and the precise magnitude of improvements in compressive strength is not yet quantified.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of pure (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 and one set with 3–5 vol% Cu added. Process both sets under identical synthesis and thermomechanical conditions. Test the samples under standardized applied-field and pressure-field conditions while monitoring mechanical integrity (via compressive strength tests) and caloric performance (e.g., measurement of entropy change and transformation temperature).
measurements: Compressive strength (e.g., via standard compression tests)
Caloric effect metrics (entropy change, transformation temperature, etc.)
Fracture surface and crack propagation analysis (microscopy)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Cu-doped samples do not show a statistically significant improvement in compressive strength and reduced cracking relative to the baseline, or if the caloric measurements differ adversely from the baseline (i.e., any significant reduction in the caloric effect), then the hypothesis will be considered falsified.
